title: Into the Void: Understanding Online Health Information in Low-Web Data Languages
benchmark_measurement: The paper analyzes search results from YouTube and TikTok for health-related queries in low-web data languages. Regarding religion, it measures the prevalence and characteristics of religious content (e.g., advice, prayer videos, spiritual terms) returned in these search results, particularly for mental health topics.
findings: For health queries in Amharic and Tigrinya, search results on YouTube and TikTok are frequently dominated by nutritional and religious advice. This is especially prominent for mental health queries, which primarily return religious content such as teachings from religious leaders and prayer videos. Salient terms in search results include religious and spiritual words like 'devil', 'evil spell', 'Islam', and 'God'. The study suggests a tendency among users in these language communities to engage with religious content when seeking health information.
